newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt to win if UK stays out of EMU - Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt to win if UK stays out of EMU - Deutsche.

text.p: Rolf Breuer, chief executive designate of Deutsche Bank AG, said Germany could gain ground as a centre for financial services if Britain decides to stay outside the planned European single currency.

In an interview with the n-tv news channel to be aired on Sunday, Breuer urged German banks to be ready on January 1, 1999 for the launch of euro and said the country's financial capital Frankfurt could attract new business.
"(If) a strong competitor rules itself out, then others will take advantage -- including Frankfurt," Breuer said in extracts from the interview released by n-tv.
Breuer said he was certain that Germany would join the European monetary union (EMU) at the planned outset in 1999.
Commenting on the development of Frankfurt as a financial services centre, Breuer said the city had made up a lot of ground in the past five years and had good prospects.
"We started very late and from far back. But we have gained in tempo and have now reached a level where we don't have to feel inferior to other financial centres," he said.
Breuer said that Frankfurt's reputation had won out through the stability of the mark currency, but the reluctance of Germans to invest in shares remained a handicap.
Frankfurt, while the equal of any continental financial capital, still needed to catch up on London in attracting international investment, he said.
